title: Moments of Genuine Connection (MGCs) https://davestuartjr.com/tracking-attempted-moments-of-genuine-connection-mgc-dsjr-one-stop-shop-2
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: This guide unpacks Moments of Genuine Connection, the first of Dave Stuart Jr.'s ten Will to Learn strategies and the foundation of his approach to Teacher Credibility. An MGC is a brief, 30-to-60-second one-on-one interaction in which a teacher attempts to signal to a student that they are valued, known, and respected, tracked on a printed roster so the effort scales across 100+ students. Stuart distinguishes connecting with students as a person from connecting as a learner, arguing both are necessary for full Credibility, and offers real classroom scripts he has used with shy, struggling, or overlooked students. The guide closes with a practical FAQ covering frequency, emotional exhaustion, what to write on the tracker, and how to recover when an MGC attempt seems to fail.
points: An MGC is defined precisely as 30 to 60 seconds in which the teacher attempts to communicate to a student that they are valued, known, and/or respected, brief enough to be sustainable across a full teaching load.
Stuart tracks MGCs on a printed clipboard roster because keeping 100+ students' relationship status in his head is impossible, aiming to reach every student at least once per month.
He distinguishes connecting with a student as a PERSON from connecting with them as a LEARNER, arguing that neglecting either one damages the student's overall sense of the teacher's Credibility.
He frames failed or awkward MGC attempts not as one-and-done failures but as a long-term investing strategy, where repeated attempts raise the odds a student eventually receives the signal.
quotes: A moment of genuine connection (MGC) is simple: 30 to 60 seconds in which I, as the teacher, attempt to communicate to a student that I value, know, and/or respect them.
Because I cannot possibly mentally keep track of attempting MGCs with 100+ students each semester, I keep track of these on a printed out roster that I keep on a clipboard.

If I only connect with them as a person, they may come to believe that I'm a caring person but not a capable teacher. If I only connect with them as a learner, they may come to believe that I only care about their work in my class and not about them as a person overall.
First, like every worthwhile teaching strategy, MGC attempts are a practicable, improvable skill. There are weak MGC attempts and strong MGC attempts.

More importantly, you have to view tracking attempted MGCs as a strategy akin to long-term investing. With each series you complete, the likelihood of a student receiving the valued/respected/known signal into their heart increases.
Questions posed with curiosity and eye contact are a fine method for indicating to someone that you value them, that you want to know them, and that you respect them.
